Intracerebroventricular (icv) injections are used to deliver medications directly into the brain. Metformin and AICAR (all-insulin-activating protein) are examples of such medications.

When you inject these substances into the ewe's cerebroventricle, they can affect various physiological processes throughout the body. AMPK (adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase) is an enzyme that plays a role in energy production within cells, including those in the brain.

Research suggests that icv injections of metformin or AICAR may influence melatonin secretion. Melatonin is a hormone produced by the pineal gland that regulates sleep-wake cycles and other physiological processes. AMPK activation has been linked to modulating melatonin secretion.

The exact mechanisms through which metformin or AICAR affect melatonin levels are not yet fully understood, but it is thought that AMPK may be involved in this process. This could occur either directly within the pineal gland or indirectly by influencing other physiological pathways that regulate melatonin production.

Overall, these findings suggest a potential role for AMPK on the secretion of melatonin, which may act through the paraventricular nucleus and/or directly in the pineal gland. Taken together, these results indicate that AMPK may be involved in modulating melatonin secretion.
